title: Dynamical regime and parameter identification of a whole-brain MPR model from resting-state fMRI with a noise-aware physics-informed neural network
trl: Phase 4 complete on proposal r14 (published 2026-11-11; judge: Concept & Feasibility 78, forecast Overall 3)
executive_summary: We ask what the resting-state BOLD of one subject determines about a whole-brain Montbrio-Pazo-Roxin (MPR) model: its dynamical regime, bistable or monostable, and a low-dimensional set of parameters (G, the noise level, and eta_i = eta_0 + a m_i along a fixed map). A synthetic stage first establishes which BOLD statistics identify the regime and recover the parameters; the two configurations are then fitted to the same real data by forward simulation against a linear floor, reliability is measured across seeds and sessions, and a hybrid PINN is compared with the forward benchmark and tested as a reconstructor of regional states. Equations are those of r12; the noise parametrisation, the PINN forcing term, the dynamic statistics and the monostable configuration are owed. Source: proposal r13.

novelty.problem_statement: Regime-assumed estimates of regional excitabilities $\eta_i$, of unknown reliability, in whole-brain MPR models fitted to single-subject resting-state fMRI

central.text: Regime-assumed estimates of regional excitabilities $\eta_i$, of unknown reliability, in whole-brain MPR models fitted to single-subject resting-state fMRI

causes.text: Static FC fits do not discriminate regional switching between states from noise around one equilibrium, and whether resting-state BOLD requires nonlinear, let alone multistable, dynamics is contested
Functional features alone (FC, FCD) carry insufficient information to determine regional excitabilities, so fits improve while regional estimates vary across optimization runs
The regime is fixed by assumption before fitting, and noise, when estimated, is estimated conditional on it, without testing how the regime verdict depends on either

effects.text: Mechanistic readings of fitted MPR models, such as neuronal cascades, rest on a dynamical regime the data have not been shown to support
Regional parameters of whole-brain models are read as subject-level markers, yet for the MPR model their test-retest reliability is unknown

pillars.name: P1. Regime decided by the data
pillars.summary: Fit the bistable and the monostable configuration of the same MPR model to the same data and decide the regime from held-out dynamic statistics, against a linear floor, along a noise grid
pillars.details: Answers DC1 and DC3. Both configurations are fitted because fixing one before fitting is what DC3 names (Rabuffo et al. 2021, l.162; Hashemi et al. 2024, l.157; Ziaeemehr et al. 2025, l.490; Lavanga et al. 2023 fix the node bistable and fit G and the noise variance under it). The regime is read from dynamic statistics because a static FC fit does not discriminate it (Nozari et al. 2024 against Forrester et al. 2024). The noise level $\sigma_\xi$ is fixed at the value of Hashemi et al. (2024), $\sigma_\xi^2=0.03$, and the regime verdict is reported along a $\sigma_\xi$ grid covering its variance and standard-deviation readings, as Ziaeemehr et al. (2025, Fig. 7 supplements 6-7) evaluate estimation across noise levels. Configurations follow the literature convention: decoupled node in the bistable range of $\eta$, network switching judged by FCD variance (Hashemi et al. 2024).

pillars.name: P2. Identifiability before any real fit
pillars.summary: Establish on synthetic data, before any real fit, which BOLD statistics identify the regime and recover $G$ and $\eta_i$, using functional and spatio-temporal features
pillars.details: Answers DC2. FC and FCD alone do not determine regional excitabilities (Hashemi et al. 2024, l.141 and l.317; Ziaeemehr et al. 2025, l.241, Fig. 7 supplement 3), while G is recovered from FC/FCD (Ziaeemehr et al. 2025, Fig. 7 supplements 4-5). Features: FC, FCD and its variance, and scale-free regional statistics (skewness, kurtosis, autocorrelation of the normalised series); absolute mean and variance are excluded because preprocessing and arbitrary scanner units remove them (Ziaeemehr et al. 2025, l.315). Whether free $\eta_i$ or the map $\eta_0+a\,m_i$ is the estimation target is decided here, not assumed. Tolerance: posterior z-score and shrinkage (Betancourt 2014; Hashemi et al. 2024), spread across seeds and initial values; initial thresholds |z| <= 2 and s >= 0.5 are the authors’ proposal, revisited with the pilot. Synthetic BOLD receives the same preprocessing as the chosen real dataset.

pillars.name: P3. Reliability measured, not assumed
pillars.summary: Measure the reliability of $G$ and $\eta_i$ across seeds, initial values and sessions of the same subject, instead of assuming it
pillars.details: Answers DC2 and EF2. Runs and sessions are distinct: Wischnewski et al. (2025) measure reliability across 30 repeated optimization runs per subject (poor to fair for high-dimensional parameters, phase oscillators); Saberi et al. (cuBNM, eLife Reviewed Preprint) measure HCP day 1 against day 2 in 217 subjects with a node-heterogeneous reduced Wong-Wang model, parameters poor-to-fair. For the MPR model no reviewed source reports test-retest reliability (bounded search owed). Sessions are used when the subject has a second one; otherwise halves of the session.

pillars.name: P4. Noise-aware PINN as transversal estimator
pillars.summary: A PINN with a noise forcing term, needed in both regimes, that estimates the parameters and reconstructs the hidden trajectories $r_i(t)$, $V_i(t)$ and the regional states lasting long enough for BOLD to resolve
pillars.details: Transversal tool: provides estimates and states to P1 and P3, and state reconstruction as its own contribution. Without forcing the MPR has only fixed points (Montbrió et al. 2015, l.129), so a noise-free network rests at one in either regime; the forcing term is therefore needed in both. Among estimators used with whole-brain MPR models (sweep, CMA-ES, simulation-based inference) the PINN is the one that returns hidden trajectories; stochastic DCM and Kalman-type filters also estimate hidden states in other models (Li et al. 2011; Razi et al. 2015). The BOLD is a low-pass observation, so only states lasting seconds are recoverable. PINN training is sensitive to loss balance and time scales (Rohrhofer et al. 2023). Form and penalty of the forcing term: pending deliberation (proposed: per-region Fourier basis penalised to the power of a band-limited noise of variance $\sigma_\xi^2$).

hypotheses.title: Identifiability on synthetic data (required gate)
hypotheses.statement: On synthetic BOLD of both configurations, preprocessed as the real data (detrending, GSR), FC, FCD and scale-free regional statistics identify the regime and recover $G$ and free $\eta_i$, or else the map $\eta_0+a\,m_i$, within the pilot tolerance, across the $\sigma_\xi$ grid
hypotheses.evidence: Not yet tested. Also decides the estimation target (free eta_i or map) and the number of volumes, hence the dataset.

hypotheses.title: Dynamical regime on real data
hypotheses.statement: On real single-subject BOLD, bistable and monostable fits differ in held-out dynamic statistics by more than seed and, when available, session variability, read against a linear floor and reported along the $\sigma_\xi$ grid
hypotheses.evidence: Not yet tested; read only after H1 holds. Linear floor model owed.

hypotheses.title: Reliability on real data
hypotheses.statement: Repeated fits with different seeds, initial values and, when available, a second session give the same $G$ and $\eta_i$ within their spread, with the mapped parametrisation $\eta_i=\eta_0+a\,m_i$ as comparison
hypotheses.evidence: Not yet tested; read only after H1 holds.

hypotheses.title: The PINN as estimator and reconstructor of states
hypotheses.statement: A noise-aware PINN recovers on synthetic data the fraction of time each region spends in each state, and on real data its estimates give an FC no worse than sweep and CMA-ES under a declared simulation budget
hypotheses.evidence: Not yet tested; forcing term pending deliberation. Can fail without affecting H1 to H3.

layers.name: Layer 1: Data instance
layers.description: Structural connectome A and regional BOLD of one subject; every instance-dependent value lives in Section 3.1.

nodes.name: Structural connectome A
nodes.desc: Fibre counts without diagonal, normalised to a maximum of 1.

nodes.name: Measured FC
nodes.desc: Pearson correlation over P=N(N-1)/2 pairs, after the instance's preprocessing.

nodes.name: Regional map m_i
nodes.desc: Group T1w/T2w myelin ratio (HCP), averaged per Desikan-Killiany region and standardised; uncovered regions take m_i=0.

layers.name: Layer 2: Neural dynamics (MPR)
layers.description: One MPR neural mass per region, coupled through A without delays (Eqs. 1-2).

nodes.name: eta_0, a (estimated)
nodes.desc: eta_i = eta_0 + a m_i (Eq. 15); eta_0 starts at -4.6; free eta_i only as the H3 control.

nodes.name: G (estimated)
nodes.desc: Global coupling, parametrised around G0 = 1/mean row sum of A.

nodes.name: Fixed: Delta=0.7, J=14.5, tau_m=1 ms
nodes.desc: From Rabuffo et al. (2021); tau_m=10 ms as sensitivity.

layers.name: Layer 3: Hemodynamics and BOLD
layers.description: Balloon-Windkessel with SPM12/Zeidman values: state equations (Eqs. 6-9), BOLD equation (Eq. 10) and its coefficients (Eq. 11).

nodes.name: Balloon-Windkessel
nodes.desc: States s_i, f_i, nu_i, q_i normalised to rest; integrated from rest at t=0 (first volume) with log f, log nu, log q to keep them positive while the solution stays positive (chi bounds the input); kappa=0.64, gamma=0.32, tau_h=2.00 s, alpha=0.32, E0=0.4; Friston 2003 as sensitivity.

nodes.name: k1, k2, k3
nodes.desc: Functions of B0, TE and E0 (Stephan 2007; Heinzle 2016).

layers.name: Layer 4: Hybrid PINN
layers.description: Network t -> (r, V) of every region; loss = physics + data + prior (Eqs. 14-23).

nodes.name: Network
nodes.desc: 3 hidden layers of 100 tanh units, Glorot, softplus on r.

nodes.name: Optimiser
nodes.desc: Adam 1e-3 with stepwise decay; optional L-BFGS polish.

layers.name: Layer 5: Evaluation
layers.description: rho_FC against noise ceilings and benchmarks; synthetic recovery, identifiability and regime checks.

nodes.name: rho_FC
nodes.desc: Pearson over P pairs; Fisher z only as sensitivity.

nodes.name: Ceilings
nodes.desc: Seed ceiling always; session ceiling if the instance has a second session.

nodes.name: Benchmarks
nodes.desc: Parameter sweep and CMA-ES fitting the same three parameters (H1).

nodes.name: Synthetic recovery
nodes.desc: Known eta_0, a, G and hidden trajectories r_i, V_i recovered before real data are interpreted (H2).

nodes.name: Regime comparison
nodes.desc: Bistable versus monostable range of eta (H4).

input_domain.name: Time
input_domain.definition: t in [t_0, t_1], scaled to [-1, 1] as network input
input_domain.description: The network maps time to the states of every region.

parameters.name: Regions
parameters.rule: Set by the parcellation of the instance

parameters.name: Collocation points
parameters.rule: Random instants for the physics residual

output_range.name: Neural states
output_range.description: Firing rate (positive via softplus) and mean membrane potential of each region.

conversion_mapping.title: Neural state to BOLD
conversion_mapping.equation: z_i = chi (r_i - mean r_i) (Eq. 5) -> Balloon-Windkessel (Eqs. 6-9) -> y_i (Eq. 10)
conversion_mapping.notes: The scale chi is set in the simulation stage.

core_equations.name: MPR firing rate
core_equations.description: Population firing rate of region i.

core_equations.name: MPR membrane potential with coupling
core_equations.latex: \tau_m \dot V_i = V_i^2 + \eta_i - (\pi \tau_m r_i)^2 + \tau_m J r_i + \tau_m G \sum_j A_{ij} r_j
core_equations.description: Mean membrane potential of region i, coupled through A.

core_equations.name: Neurovascular input
core_equations.description: Deviation of the firing rate from its time mean drives the hemodynamics.

variables.desc: Input scale (set in the simulation stage)

core_equations.name: Vasodilatory signal
core_equations.description: Signal driven by z_i = chi (r_i - mean r_i), with decay and flow feedback.

core_equations.name: Blood inflow
core_equations.description: Normalised inflow integrates the vasodilatory signal.

core_equations.name: Venous volume
core_equations.description: Balloon: volume changes with inflow minus outflow.

core_equations.name: Deoxyhaemoglobin
core_equations.description: Delivery minus expulsion of deoxyhaemoglobin; E(f) = 1-(1-E0)^(1/f), so E(1) = E0.

core_equations.name: BOLD signal
core_equations.description: BOLD from deoxyhemoglobin q_i and volume nu_i.

variables.desc: Resting venous blood volume fraction (0.02); written V_0 in Friston 2003 and Stephan 2007
Functions of B0, TE and E0

core_equations.name: FC similarity
core_equations.description: Pearson correlation of simulated and measured FC over the P upper-triangle pairs.

core_equations.name: Physics loss
core_equations.description: Squared normalised residuals of the dimensionless MPR equations at K=4096 collocation times resampled every Adam iteration.

core_equations.name: Data loss
core_equations.description: Compares the pattern of the FC, not its level.

core_equations.name: Prior
core_equations.description: Gaussian prior on the estimated parameters.

optimization_problems.name: Joint training of network, eta and G
constraints: Each term divided by a fixed scale computed before training, never by a value taken from training
lambda chosen in [0, 1] with a sensitivity grid
Gaussian prior on eta_i (sigma_eta=1) and G (sigma_G=0.5 G0)
optimization_problems.description: Physics residual of the dimensionless Eqs. 17-18 over K=4096 resampled collocation times (Eq. 21), data term 1 - rho_FC (Eq. 22) and Gaussian prior (Eq. 23); total loss Eq. 16.

contribution_type.why: r14 reframes the question as what one subject's resting BOLD determines about an MPR whole-brain model (regime, G, eta_i). It still delivers a plan: H1 is a synthetic gate, the data are one subject with T=300 volumes, and the PINN reconstruction (H4) is untested. The decisive items are H1 ('required gate'), Eqs. (24)-(25) (forcing term, new in r14) and Section 7 ('not validated here').

General.why: Method (Eqs. 14-25), four hypotheses and CMA-ES/sweep/linear-floor baselines fit the template, but the method is unvalidated and the data are a single subject.

Theory.why: No theorem. The Fourier-coefficient variance of Eq. (25) and the spectral-bias estimate in Section 7 are short derivations, not a proof contribution.

Use-Inspired.why: Perturbation and treatment uses are explicitly future work and motivation (Section 1, last paragraph); no real use case drives the design.

Concept & Feasibility.why: A new framing (inference of regime and reliability, not fit) with a feasibility gate (H1) and a first diagnostic run (rho_FC 0.72 with eta barely moving). Claims are plans, not yet supported.

Negative Results.why: H2 and H3 are framed so that failure is informative, and H4 can fail alone. Nothing is analysed yet, and the first-run failure is labelled an implementation diagnostic, not evidence.
